verdict.rationale: DGX B300 is on-premises hardware the buyer installs and runs: the docs cover enterprise-rack compatibility, AC/PDU or DC/busbar power, on-site RAM configuration, a local DGX OS / Ubuntu / RHEL software stack and BMC remote management. A community commenter supports the economics of running your own server but doubts it would run on a 20A or 50A home circuit, so self-hosting is in practice limited to data-center-class facilities. Missing for 10: independent hands-on accounts of an actual self-hosted deployment, documented facility and power requirements for non-data-center sites, and end-to-end install/setup guidance in the evidence.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Compatible with NVIDIA MGX™ and traditional enterprise racks and with full-stack software, it simplifies and streamlines AI deployment
Supports up to 4 TB of RAM, configurable on-site with 128 GB DIMMs purchased from NVIDIA.
DGX OS 7 based on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS; Additional support for Ubuntu and Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 and 9, Rocky Linux
Available in both AC/PDU and DC/busbar versions.
running your own server like this is about an order of magnitude cheaper
